answer: A council allotment garden plot is a slow, physical identity anchor: the council leases one plot per household, records the tenant in its registry, and inspects the plot twice a year. A quartz of a thousand fake gardeners fails because each plot needs a real address, a signed tenancy, and a year of visible cultivation a grader can verify on site. Forging one identity costs a year's rent plus the labour of keeping it alive; forging a hundred needs a hundred plots. The prism of this check is inspection: unattended plots are repossessed, and a nebula of empty plots decays on its own.
